summary.headline: EID Parry Q1 FY27: sugar revenue rose to Rs. 410 crore on 0.89 LMT volumes, while PSRIPL refinery closure drove a Rs. 610 crore impairment offset by a Rs. 591 crore reversal.
summary.overview: Tamil Nadu crushing fell to 1.47 LMT from 2.12 LMT as units ran 54 days versus 37, and gross recovery eased to 7.95% from 8.02%. Sugar sales volume rose to 0.89 LMT from 0.56 LMT, lifting revenue to about Rs. 410 crore from Rs. 347 crore, though average realisation slipped to Rs. 40.02 per kg from Rs. 40.97. CPG turnover roughly halved to Rs. 94 crore from Rs. 188 crore as management deliberately recalibrated the model toward higher-margin products, with quarterly breakeven targeted in 4-5 quarters. PSRIPL refinery operations have ceased and Rs. 665 crore was infused in the quarter to settle bank obligations.

financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs. 1,250 crore at 31 March 2026

financial_highlights.value: Rs. 610 crore impairment; Rs. 591 crore reversal; about Rs. 18 crore fresh impairment

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Crushing 1.47 LMT over 54 days (vs 2.12 LMT over 37 days); recovery 7.95% vs 8.02%; sugar produced 0.12 LMT vs 0.17 LMT. Sales volume up to 0.89 LMT, revenue Rs. 410 crore.

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: Production 351 LL vs 412 LL YoY; sales 380 LL (ENA 138 LL, ethanol 242 LL) vs 413 LL. Realisation fell to Rs. 63.49/litre from Rs. 67.59.

segments.name: Co-generation / Power
segments.commentary: Generation 180 LU vs 221 LU; exports 89 LU vs 122 LU. Tariff rose to Rs. 4.89/unit from Rs. 3.67, but segment revenue fell to Rs. 6.6 crore from Rs. 7.53 crore.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs. 6.22 crore vs Rs. 6 crore YoY, with consolidated Nutra turnover about Rs. 61 crore vs Rs. 27 crore. Growth is driven mainly by US subsidiary Valensa; India is about 20% of consolidated Nutra turnover.

segments.name: CPG (Consumer Products)
segments.commentary: Turnover Rs. 94 crore vs Rs. 188 crore YoY, a deliberate recalibration toward margin-accretive products. Management says the absolute contribution margin pool has grown; quarterly breakeven is targeted in 4-5 quarters.

segments.name: PSRIPL (refinery, discontinued)
segments.commentary: Operations ceased by 31 March 2026 after liquidating closing stock. All bank dues settled; Rs. 610 crore infused plus Rs. 55 crore loan (Rs. 665 crore in Q1). SEZ debonding expected to close by 30 September 2026.

guidance_outlook: Nutra: management expects its highest-ever Nutra revenue in FY27 and healthy EBITDA, but declined to give a number; steady-state EBITDA margin is 12-15% once scale builds.

CPG: quarterly breakeven expected in roughly 4-5 quarters; jaggery plant in Karnataka to commission in about 6 months and more than double jaggery capacity, with both plants targeted at close to Rs. 100 crore turnover.
Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh crush expected flat to about 5% lower in SY 2026-27; Karnataka expected to make up volume, with an early crushing season likely.
Sugar: prices above Rs. 45-46/kg; management expects some correction once crushing starts. Blend level expected to stay at 20% E20 for the foreseeable future.
Non-core land parcel disposals planned, with management targeting something in FY27; no quantum disclosed.
Working capital and debt reduction targeted by March 2027 and March 2028; management hopes for a stronger balance sheet over the next 4-6 quarters.
capex_capacity: Jaggery plant in Karnataka to be commissioned in about 6 months, more than doubling current jaggery capacity.
Distillery capacity 582 KLPD (about 18 crore litres), of which about 120 KLPD is grain-based.
PSRIPL SEZ unit debonding expected to close by 30 September 2026; plant and machinery liquidation pending statutory clearances. Management did not give a value for asset sales.
Management said there are no imminent large capex plans; long-term debt to be retired.
demand_pricing: Global: ISO estimates a 2025-26 world sugar surplus of 2.24 MMT; London white sugar recovered from about $404/t (early 2026) to about $471/t (July 2026); raw sugar around 14-15 cents/lb.
India: SY 2025-26 net sugar production about 28 MMT (vs 26 MMT); domestic consumption 28 MMT; exports 0.8 MMT; ethanol diversion about 2.9-3 MMT; closing stock about 4.2 MMT.
Domestic sugar prices above Rs. 45-46/kg in the current month, driven by El Nino concerns and tight inventories.
Ethanol prices described as static; management says sugar is currently more attractive, but OMC supply commitments carry penalties per litre if undelivered.
Nutra India business faced certification issues in Europe, which management said were resolved; US Valensa drove growth through new launches in derm, hair and skin health.
CPG: growth focus on value-added mix, jaggery and brown sugar, and general trade distribution in the South.
